title: HIV, hepatitis B and C, and syphilis test
what: A blood test from a vein that looks for signs of these infections. One tube is usually enough for all four.
why: Before surgery, during pregnancy, before donating blood, at a checkup, or after a risky situation.
duration: the blood draw takes 3 to 5 minutes. Results usually take 1 to 5 days
tell_doctor: If you had a risky situation, and exactly when. The timing of the test depends on it
If you have been treated for these infections before

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: It is usually best to come fasting, or 4 to 6 hours after a light meal. Check with the lab. Water is fine.

prepare.title: Timing after a risk
prepare.text: The test may not find an infection in the first weeks. It is usually done after 3 to 6 weeks and repeated after 3 months. Your doctor will tell you when.

prepare.title: Privacy
prepare.text: Your result is confidential. In many places, you can get an HIV test anonymously and for free.

bring: Your ID, if the test is not anonymous
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tied on your arm, and the skin is cleaned with antiseptic
A quick prick, and blood fills the tube
The needle is removed, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
You get the result in person or through your doctor
A first positive test is not a diagnosis. It is always checked with another test
red_flags: If you were at risk of HIV less than 72 hours ago, see a doctor or an HIV center right away. There are medicines that help prevent infection

faq.q: How long after a risk should I get an HIV test?
faq.a: Modern tests usually detect HIV after 3 to 6 weeks. To be sure, the test is repeated after 3 months.

faq.q: Can the result be a false positive?
faq.a: Yes, for example during pregnancy or with other illnesses. That is why every positive result is checked with a second test.

faq.q: Can I get an HIV test anonymously?
faq.a: Yes. Many clinics and HIV centers offer it anonymously and for free. No ID is needed.
